summary: D-094 preserves the 18-gate denominator, correct reserved-to-named edits, status vocabulary, threshold values, implementation freeze, and D-093 subjects. It nevertheless cannot be the D-006-conforming naming act yet. D-006 requires this reviewed act itself to pin exact machine identifiers and OS versions, but D-094 supplies families and alternatives and explicitly defers exact builds/images to the first harness run. Its native-Intel procurability evidence proves access only to an opaque GitHub-hosted 4-CPU/14-GB Intel VM, not the selected 2018-class i5/i7 8-GB Mac mini; current GitHub material also supersedes the draft's 'last Intel image' premise. Finally, the rule requiring `sysctl.proc_translated = 0` mishandles Apple's documented native-process ENOENT case. Until all three are repaired and refrozen, G03/G04 remain reserved and unnamed, condition 4 remains 16 of 18 and PARTLY MET, and CONSENT is unavailable.

objections.title: The naming act still does not pin exact machines or exact OS versions
objections.finding: D-006 says the exact machine identifiers, OS versions, and cache-state protocol are pinned by the reviewed G03/G04 harness-naming act. D-086 repeats that all of those pins must exist before the reserved identifiers contribute naming progress. D-094 instead chooses `M1-class`, a `2018-class` Intel Mac mini with an unresolved `i5/i7` alternative, and generic `4 vCPU / 8 GB` Linux classes. It chooses `macOS 15 ... family` and `Ubuntu 24.04 LTS`, then expressly postpones the exact image build, Darwin build, AMI, or runner-image digest to the first harness run. Those are still classes/families, not exact identifiers and versions, and postponement contradicts the precondition for this naming act.
objections.evidence: COORD D-006: `The EXACT machine identifiers, OS versions and cache-state protocol are pinned by the G03/G04 harness-naming`. Gate-harness-naming.v3 and adopted D-086 preserve the same obligation. D-094's Pins section contains multiple CPU alternatives and no Apple model identifier, CPU SKU, storage/device identifier, cloud instance SKU, image ID, OS point release, or OS build; its next paragraph defers those values to execution.
objections.impact: The two v3 identifiers remain zero-progress reservations. Applying the proposed file-08 replacements would record a false D-006-conforming premise and prematurely change condition 4 from 16/18 PARTLY MET to 18/18 MET.
objections.requiredRepair: Pin one exact, reproducible machine per platform in the D-094 bytes: for Macs, a single model identifier and CPU/SOC SKU with RAM/storage and exact OS build; for Linux, a single instance/machine SKU and immutable image identifier with exact OS build. Remove i5/i7 and other family alternatives. Do not defer the required pins to the first run. A later runner/image refresh must be a reviewed successor rather than silent drift. Re-measure and refreeze.

objections.title: The cited Intel venue does not verify procurability of the machine D-094 selected
objections.finding: D-094's only evidence for native-Intel procurability is GitHub's `macos-15-intel` hosted label. Current GitHub documentation describes that standard runner as an Intel VM with 4 CPUs and 14 GB RAM and does not identify it as a 2018 Mac mini, an i5/i7 SKU, or an 8-GB machine. D-094 itself selects a 2018-class i5/i7 8-GB Mac mini and says a venue that does not match the class is rejected. A CPU brand string plus translation state cannot prove the selected model, CPU alternative, RAM, or storage. No separate purchase, lease, lab, or self-hosted availability evidence is supplied for the selected pin.
objections.evidence: Current official GitHub-hosted-runner specifications list `macos-15-intel` as 4 CPU / 14 GB and list both `macos-15-intel` and `macos-26-intel`: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/runners/github-hosted-runners . The live runner-images catalog likewise lists both Intel images: https://github.com/actions/runner-images . The cited 2025 announcement at https://github.com/actions/runner-images/issues/13045 established label availability but not a matching 2018 Mac-mini/8-GB venue; its 'last x86_64 image' statement is no longer current.
objections.impact: The product sign-off asserts, but does not verify, procurability of the exact representative pin D-006 requires. Therefore D-094 cannot lawfully reject the unprocurability route or count G03/G04 as named.
objections.requiredRepair: After ADV-D094-01 selects one exact Intel pin, retain auditable evidence that the same model/spec is actually procurable for repeated qualification runs and name the intended physical or self-hosted venue. If the GitHub VM is preferred, select and justify its documented runner specification rather than calling it the 2018 Mac-mini/8-GB pin, and satisfy D-006's exact-identifier requirement. Refresh the current GitHub availability recital. If a matching native-Intel pin cannot be procured, route that result through a reviewed D-006 successor and leave G03/G04 reserved, 16/18, and PARTLY MET.

objections.title: The anti-Rosetta check rejects a documented native-process result
objections.finding: D-094 twice requires `sysctl.proc_translated` to exist and equal `0`. Apple's documented algorithm treats value 1 as translated, value 0 as native when the OID exists, and ENOENT as native when the OID is absent. Requiring literal command output `0` therefore does not implement Apple's native test and can reject a genuine Intel/native process. It also leaves unspecified how command failure is distinguished from translation.
objections.evidence: Apple's `About the Rosetta translation environment` documents the `sysctlbyname("sysctl.proc_translated")` algorithm and explicitly maps ENOENT to native 0: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/Apple-Silicon/about-the-rosetta-translation-environment . D-094's procurability bullet and Cold trace paragraph both require the key itself to be `0` without the ENOENT branch.
objections.impact: The selected native-Intel runner may be unable to satisfy the naming act's own admission rule. That makes the procurability conclusion and executable cache protocol internally inconsistent even though the rule fails closed rather than silently allowing Rosetta.
objections.requiredRepair: Define a deterministic native-architecture check that records host model, CPU architecture/brand, process architecture, and the Rosetta query result. Reject value 1 and unexpected errors; accept 0 or ENOENT only when the independent host/process facts establish native Intel. Apply the same rule in both the procurability finding and cache-state trace requirements, then remeasure and refreeze.
